prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1009; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a low-speed head-on collision reported by the insured. Insured states the other vehicle crossed into their lane on a curve. No police report on file yet. Vehicle drivable, towed from scene as a precaution. Photos requested from insured.

Entry 2: Recorded statement taken from the claimant, who reports neck pain and stiffness beginning the morning after the collision. Claimant says they did not feel significant impact at the time. Claimant has not retained an attorney and states they are handling the claim directly. Advised claimant of the process for medical documentation and rental coverage.

Entry 3: Claimant confirmed they visited an urgent care clinic and were diagnosed with whiplash-type soft tissue injury. Requested discharge notes and treatment plan with the claimant's signed authorization. Claimant reports ongoing headaches and reduced range of motion in the neck. Advised that a physical therapy referral may be considered once records are reviewed.

Entry 4: Reviewed photos of both vehicles. Damage is consistent with a low-speed frontal impact, with minor bumper and hood deformation on both sides. Repair estimate received for the claimant's vehicle and is under review. Independent appraisal scheduled for the other party's vehicle.

Entry 5: Spoke again with the claimant, who has no questions about the injury claim at this time and says they feel some improvement. Medical records requested and expected within the standard response window. Reserve reviewed and adjusted to reflect the medical and repair exposure. File remains open pending records and final repair figures.
